The end is drawing near, soul, it is drawing near, and you do not care, you do not prepare. The time is growing short: rise up! The Judge is near, at the very doors. Like a dream, like a flower, the time of life runs by. Why are we troubled in vain? Come to your senses, my soul; consider the deeds you have done, and set them before your eyes, and [?] the drops of your tears. Tell your deeds and your thoughts boldly to Christ, and be justified. There has been in this life no sin, no deed, no wickedness that I, Saviour, have not committed, in mind and knowledge and choice, sinning in intention, in judgement and in deed as no one else has

Hence I was condemned, hence I, wretched one, was sentenced by my own conscience, than which nothing in the world is more forceful. Judge, my Redeemer, who know all, spare and deliver and save me, your servant. The ladder that the great one among the patriarchs once saw, my soul, is an example of the step of action and of the ascent of knowledge. If, then, you wish to live by action, knowledge and contemplation, be renewed [?]

The patriarch endured the burning heat of the day because of want, and bore the frost of the night, making good the losses day by day, shepherding, struggling, serving, so that he might win the two wives. By the two wives understand action and knowledge in contemplation: Leah as action, since she had many children; and Rachel as knowledge, since she was won by much toil. For without toil, soul, neither action nor contemplation [?]. Keep watch, my soul; be valiant like the great one among the patriarchs, so that you may acquire action together with knowledge, and be called a mind that sees God, and [?]

the unapproachable darkness in contemplation, and become a great merchant. The great one among the patriarchs, having fathered the twelve patriarchs, mystically set up for you, my soul, a ladder of ascent by action, most wisely laying down his children as rungs and their steps as ascents. Emulating Esau the hated, soul, you gave up to your supplanter the birthright of your first beauty and fell from your father's blessing; and you were supplanted twice, wretched one, in action and in knowledge. Therefore repent now. Esau was called Edom because of his extreme frenzy of lust for women; for, burning always with incontinence and stained with pleasures, he was named Edom, which means the heat of a sin-loving soul. You have heard, my soul, of Job, justified on the dunghill, but you have not emulated his courage. You did not have firmness of purpose in all that you knew, in all that you underwent, but proved impatient. He who was once on a throne is now naked on a dunghill, covered with sores; he who was rich in children and admired is suddenly childless and homeless. Yet he counted the dunghill a palace and the sores pearls. Clothed in royal rank, with diadem and purple, a man of great possessions and righteous, laden with wealth and flocks, he suddenly became poor and [?] his wealth, his glory, his kingdom [?]

If he was righteous and blameless above all, and yet did not escape the snares and pits of the deceiver, what will you do, wretched sin-loving soul, if something unexpected should befall you? I am defiled in body, stained in spirit, wholly covered with sores. But as physician, Christ, heal both through my repentance; wash me, cleanse me, rinse me; make me, my Saviour, purer than snow. Your body and your blood, Word, you offered when you were crucified for all: your body to refashion me, your blood to wash me clean. You gave up your spirit, Word, to bring me, Christ, to your Father. [?] You worked salvation in the midst of the earth, Creator, that we might be saved; of your own will you were crucified on the wood

[?] Eden, which had been closed, was opened; things above and things below, all creation, all the nations, now saved, worship you. Let the blood from your side be a font for me, and also a drink, the water of forgiveness that gushed out, so that I may be cleansed by both, anointed and drinking, having as anointing and drink, Word, your life-giving words. I am stripped of the bridal chamber; I am stripped of the wedding and of the supper too. My lamp has gone out, having no oil; the bridal chamber was shut while I slept; the supper has been eaten; and I, bound hand and foot, have been thrown outside. The Church has gained as its chalice your life-bearing side, from which the twofold stream of forgiveness and knowledge poured out for us, as a figure of the Old and the New, of the two Covenants together, Saviour.

The time of my life is short and full of toil and wickedness; but accept me in repentance and [?] in knowledge [?] a possession, not the food of the stranger; Saviour, have pity on me yourself. I am now boastful and bold of heart, idly and in vain; do not condemn me with the Pharisee. Rather grant me the humility of the tax collector, only merciful one, righteous Judge, and number me with him. I have sinned and outraged the vessel of my flesh, I know it, merciful one; but accept me in repentance and call me back to knowledge; let me not become the possession and the food of the stranger. Saviour, [?]

I have become my own idol, harming my soul with the passions, merciful one. But accept me in repentance and call me back to knowledge; let me not become the possession and the food of the stranger; Saviour, have pity on me yourself. I have not listened to your voice; I have disobeyed your Scripture, Lawgiver. But accept me in repentance and call me back to knowledge; let me not become the possession and the food of the stranger; Saviour, have pity on me yourself.

Having pursued a bodiless way of life in the body, holy one, you have truly [?] very great grace from God; protect those who faithfully honour you. Therefore we entreat you to deliver us by your prayers from every kind of temptation. Dragged down into the depth of great wrongs, you were not [?], but by better reasoning you ran up, plainly through action, to the very highest virtue, and wonderfully, Mary, you astonished the angelic natures. Andrew, glory of [?], do not [?] by your prayers, standing near and entreating the Trinity beyond divinity, that we may be redeemed from punishment, we who with longing [?] you as our protector [?]

You both give birth and remain a virgin, and through both you remain a virgin by nature. He who was born renews the laws of nature, and the womb conceives without labour. Where God wills, the order of nature is overcome; for he does whatever he pleases. Ode 5. The Irmos. As I rise early from the night, Lover of mankind, enlighten me, I pray, and guide me too in your commandments, and teach me, Saviour, to do your will. I have always passed my life in night; for the night of sin has become darkness and deep mist for me. But make me, Saviour, a son of the day. Imitating Reuben, I, wretched one, have carried out an unlawful and lawless plan against God most high, defiling my bed as he defiled his father's.

I confess to you, Christ the King: I have sinned, I have sinned, like the brothers who once sold Joseph, the fruit of purity and chastity. The righteous soul was betrayed by his kinsmen; the sweet one was sold into slavery as a figure of the Lord. But you, my soul, have sold yourself wholly to your evils. Imitate Joseph the righteous and his chaste mind, wretched and reprobate soul, and do not live in licentiousness, forever transgressing with irrational impulses. Though Joseph once dwelt in a pit, Master and Lord, it was as a figure of your burial and resurrection. But I—what such offering will I ever bring you? You have heard, soul, of the ark of Moses, carried on the waters and waves of the river as in a chamber of old, escaping the bitter act of Pharaoh's decree.

You have not slain the Egyptian mind as great Moses did, O soul. How then, tell me, will you come through repentance to dwell in the wilderness that is free of passions? Picture to yourself the rod of Moses, O soul, striking the sea and making the deep solid, a type of the divine Cross. Through it you too will be able to accomplish great things. Aaron offered God fire that was blameless and without guile. But Hophni and Phinehas, like you, O soul, brought God a strange and defiled life. I have become as hard of will as bitter Pharaoh, O Master: a Jannes and Jambres in soul and body, and a mind sunk beneath the waters. But help [?]

Wretch that I am, I am mired in the mud in my mind. Wash me, Master, in the font of my tears, I beg you, and make the robe of my flesh as white as snow. If I search out my deeds, Savior, I see that I have gone beyond every human being in sins, because I sinned with full knowledge and understanding, not [?]
Spare, spare your creature, Lord. I have sinned; forgive me. For you alone are pure by nature, and no one else besides you is [?]

For my sake, though you are God, you took on my form. You showed wonders: you healed lepers and made paralytics strong, and with the touch of your hem, Savior, you stopped the flow of the woman with the hemorrhage. [?] so that you may be delivered from scourges, and hear from him: “Your faith has saved you.” Imitate the woman who was bent to the ground, O soul. Come, fall at the feet of Jesus, so that he may set you upright and you may walk straight in the paths of the Lord. [?]

All-blessed one, with incomparable love you longed to venerate the wood of life, and you were granted your desire. Grant me too, then, to attain the glory above. When you crossed the stream of the Jordan, you found rest and escaped the painful pleasure of the flesh. Deliver us from it as well by your prayers, holy one.
Wise Andrew, best of shepherds, chosen above others, with great longing and fear I beg that through your intercessions I may attain salvation and eternal life.

Glory. We glorify you, O Trinity, the one God. Holy, holy, holy are you, Father, Son and Spirit, simple essence, unity forever worshipped. Both now. Theotokion. Incorrupt one, who knew no husband, virgin mother: from you God, who created the ages, clothed himself in my clay and united human nature to himself. Ode 6. The Irmos. I cried with my whole heart to the compassionate God, and he heard me from the lowest Hades and brought my soul up from corruption. Savior, I offer you in purity the tears of my eyes and groans from the depths, as my heart cries out: O God, I have sinned against you; be merciful to me. You have turned away from your Lord, O soul, like Dathan and Abiram. But cry “Spare me!” with your whole heart, so that the chasm of the earth does not swallow you up. Like a frenzied heifer, O soul, you have become like Ephraim. Rescue your life like a gazelle from the snares, giving your mind wings by action and contemplation. Let the hand of Moses assure us, O soul, that God can whiten and cleanse a leprous life. Do not despair of yourself, even if you are leprous. The waves of my offenses, Savior, have turned back and suddenly covered me, as the Red Sea once covered the Egyptians and their captains.

Your will was ungrateful, O soul, like Israel's of old. For you senselessly preferred the greedy, pleasure-loving appetite of the passions to the divine manna. [?] You preferred swine's flesh and cauldrons and Egyptian food to the food of heaven, my soul, like the ungrateful people of old in the wilderness. You valued the wells of Canaanite thoughts, O soul, above the spring in the rock, from which the river of wisdom pours forth streams of theology. When Moses your servant struck the rock with his rod, he prefigured your life-giving side, Savior, from which we all draw the drink of life. Search out and spy out, O soul, as Joshua son of Nun did, what the land of the inheritance is like, and settle in it by keeping the law. Arise and fight down the passions of the flesh, as Joshua fought Amalek, and keep conquering the Gibeonites, your deceitful thoughts. Cross over the flowing nature of time, as the ark once did, and take possession of that land of promise, O soul; God commands it. As you saved Peter when he cried out, Savior, come quickly and save me too. Rescue me from the beast: stretch out your hand and bring me up from the depth of sin. I know you as a calm harbor, Master, Christ. Come quickly and rescue me from the unfathomable depths of sin and despair. I am the royal coin, Savior, that you lost long ago. Light your lamp, your Forerunner, O Word, and seek and find your image. Of the Holy Woman. To quench the flame of the passions, Mary, you poured out streams of tears unceasingly, your soul on fire. Grant their grace to me too, your servant. You gained heavenly freedom from passion through the loftiest way of life on earth. Therefore, by your intercessions, entreat that those who hymn you may be delivered from the passions.
Andrew, I know you to be shepherd and presiding bishop of Crete and intercessor for the whole world. I run to you and cry: Rescue me, Father, from the depth of [?]

[?] in persons, and I am a unity, one in nature,” say the Father, the Son and the divine Spirit. Both now. Theotokion. Your womb bore God, who took a form like ours. Entreat him as Creator of all, Theotokos, that by your intercessions we may be justified. Kontakion, idiomelon. Plagal tone 2. My soul, my soul, arise! Why are you sleeping? The end is drawing near, and you will be thrown into confusion. Come to your senses, then, so that Christ God may spare you, who is present everywhere and fills all things.

The devil saw that Christ's place of healing was open, and that health was springing from it for Adam. He suffered and was stricken, and lamenting as one in danger, he cried out to his friends: “What shall I do to the Son of Mary? The Bethlehemite is killing me, he who is present everywhere and fills all things.” The Synaxarion. On the same day, following ancient tradition, we also sing the service of the Great Canon. This canon, truly the greatest of canons, was composed and written with more excellence and skill than any other by our father among the saints Andrew, archbishop of Crete, who is also called the Jerusalemite. He came from Damascus. In his fourteenth year he was sent to a school of grammar and trained in the general curriculum. Then he went to Jerusalem and took up the monastic life. Living there in holiness and love of God, in a quiet and untroubled life, he left to the Church of God many other profitable writings, both sermons and canons, and showed himself especially rich in his festal works. Among many others, he also composed the present Great Canon, which holds boundless compunction. He collected and gathered the whole history of the Old and New Testaments and from it composed the present song, that is, from Adam all the way to the ascension of Christ himself and the preaching of the apostles. Through it he urges every soul to emulate and imitate, as far as it can, all that is good in the history and to flee all that is evil, and always to run back to God through repentance, through tears and confession, and of course through every other way of pleasing him. Moreover, it flows so smoothly and melodiously that it can soften even the hardest soul and rouse it to come back to its senses and to the good, if only it is sung with a contrite heart and fitting attention. He wrote it at the time when the great Sophronius, patriarch of Jerusalem, wrote the Life of Mary of Egypt. For this Life too holds out boundless compunction and gives much comfort to those who have fallen and who sin, if only they are willing to turn away from evil. In the Greek books: “living.” In the Greek books: “recovery.” In the Greek books: “be sung.”

For the following reason these were appointed to be sung and read on this present day. Holy Lent is drawing near its end. So that people do not grow slack, become more negligent about the spiritual contests and give up self-restraint as in everything else, the great Andrew, like a trainer, uses the stories in the Great Canon to tell of the virtue of good men and, in turn, the straying of the wicked. In this way, so to speak, he makes those who are toiling more courageous and ready to strain manfully toward what lies ahead. The holy Sophronius, through his extraordinary account, makes them self-controlled once more and rouses them toward God, so that they do not fall away or despair, even if they have been caught in some transgressions until now. For the story of the Egyptian woman shows how great God's love for humanity and compassion are toward those who choose with their whole soul to turn back from their former offenses. One might say that it is called the Great Canon because of its thoughts and arguments themselves, for its author is fertile and composes them excellently. It is also called great because, while the other canons have about thirty troparia or a little more, this one runs to two hundred and fifty, and each one distills unspeakable delight. Fittingly and appropriately, then, this great Canon, which also holds great compunction, has been placed in the great fast of the Forty Days. Our same father Andrew was the first to bring this most excellent and greatest Canon, together with the account of the holy Mary, to Constantinople, when he came from Theodore, patriarch of Jerusalem, to the Sixth Council to give [?] help. At that time, while still among the monks, he fought excellently against the Monothelites. He was then enrolled in the clergy of the Church in Constantinople, and afterward he was appointed deacon and director of the orphanage there. A little later he became archbishop of Crete. Later still [?] he arrived at the place called Eresos in Mytilene and departed to the Lord, having had his full share of his own throne. By his intercessions, O God, have mercy on us. (Then the Beatitudes with the [?]

[?] of his repentance; make me too worthy, unworthy as I am. Verse: Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom. You hear, my soul, of Manoah long ago, who saw God in a vision and then received from a barren woman the fruit of the promise. Let us imitate his piety. Verse: Blessed are those who mourn, for they. You have emulated the slackness of Samson, O soul, and shorn off the glory of your works. Through love of pleasure you have betrayed your chaste and blessed life to the foreigners. Verse: Blessed are the meek, for they. He who once conquered the foreigners with the jawbone of an ass is now found to be the prey of passionate lust. But flee, my soul, from imitating his deed, his [?]

Verse: Blessed are the merciful, for they. You know the courage of Jael, my soul, who once drove a stake through Sisera and brought about salvation. You hear of the tent peg, by which the Cross is pictured for you. Verse: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they.

Verse: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they. Consider Gideon's fleece, my soul; receive the dew from heaven. Stoop like a dog and drink the water that flowed from the law when the letter was wrung out. Verse: Blessed are those who are persecuted. My soul, through lack of sense you have drawn on yourself the condemnation of Eli the priest, allowing the passions to do lawless things in you, as he allowed his children to do. Verse: Blessed are you when they revile you. Among the Judges, my soul, a Levite cut up his own wife limb by limb and divided her among the twelve tribes, so that the lawless abomination of Benjamin might be exposed to all.

Verse: Rejoice and be glad, for your reward. Hannah, the lover of chastity, as she prayed, moved her lips in praise, but her voice was not heard. And yet, though she was barren, she bore a son, [?] of her prayer.

Verse: Remember us, Lord, when you come. Hannah's son, the great Samuel, whom Ramathaim reared in the house of the Lord, was counted among the Judges. Emulate him, my soul, and judge [?] before those of others.

Verse: Remember us, Holy One, when you come. David, chosen as king, was royally anointed from the horn of divine myrrh. So you, my soul, if you desire the kingdom above, anoint yourself with tears as with myrrh. Verse: Remember us, Holy One, when. Have mercy on your creature, merciful one. Pity the work of your hands, and spare all who have sinned, and me too, who more than all have disregarded your commandments. Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit. The one without beginning, the Begotten and the Proceeding: I worship the Father who begets, I glorify the Son who is begotten, and I hymn the Holy Spirit, who shines forth together with the Father and the Son.

We worship your Offspring, who was born beyond nature, Mother of God, and we do not divide the natural glory of your Child. For though he is one in person, he is confessed as twofold in natures. Ode 7. The Irmos. We have sinned, we have transgressed, we have done wrong before you. We have not kept your commands or done as you commanded us. But do not hand us over to the end, O God of the fathers. I have sinned, I have offended, and I have set aside your commandment. For I was brought forth in sins and have added a wound to my bruises. But have mercy on me in your compassion, O God of the fathers. I have confessed the secrets of my heart to you, my judge. See my humiliation, see also my affliction, and attend to my judgment. Have mercy on me yourself in your compassion, O God of the fathers. When Saul once lost his father's donkeys, O soul, he found the kingdom by the way [?]

David the forefather once sinned doubly, my soul: he was shot by the arrow of adultery and caught by the spear of the penalty for murder. But you are sick with deeds heavier than these, through the willful [?]

David once joined one lawless act to another: he mixed adultery with murder. Yet he at once showed a double repentance. But you, O soul, have done worse things and have not repented before God. David once set up a hymn, writing it as if painting an icon, and in it he condemns the deed he had done, crying out: “Have mercy on me, for against you alone have I sinned, the God of all. Cleanse me yourself.” When the ark was being carried on a cart and the ox stumbled, Uzzah merely touched it and felt the wrath of God. Flee his presumption, O soul, and revere divine things rightly. You have heard how Absalom rose up against nature. You know his abominable deeds, by which he defiled the bed of his father David. Yet you have imitated his passionate and pleasure-loving impulses [?]

The wonderful Solomon, who was full of the grace of wisdom, once did evil in the sight of God and turned away from him. To him you have likened your accursed life, O soul. Drawn away by the pleasures of his passions, he became defiled. Alas! The lover of wisdom became a lover of harlots and a stranger to God. You have imitated him in mind, O soul, through shameful indulgence. You have rivaled Rehoboam, who disregarded his father's counsel, and also the wicked servant Jeroboam, the apostate of old, O soul. But flee from imitating them, and cry to God: I have sinned; have pity on [?]
me. Alas! You have become a lodging for fleshly defilements and a shameful vessel of the passions. But flee from imitating them, and tell God your sins [?]

Elijah once burned up Jezebel's fifties, when he destroyed the prophets of shame to put Ahab to shame. But flee from imitating the two of them, O soul, and be strong. Heaven was shut against you, O soul, and a famine sent by God overtook you, when, like Ahab of old, you disobeyed the words of Elijah the Tishbite. But imitate the widow of Zarephath and feed the prophet's soul. By your own choice you have heaped up the crimes of Manasseh, setting up the passions as abominations and multiplying offenses, O soul. But emulate his repentance fervently and acquire compunction. I fall down before you, and I bring you my words as tears. I have sinned as no harlot ever sinned, and I have transgressed as no one else on earth. But have pity on your creature, Master, and call me back. I have buried your image and corrupted your commandment. All its beauty has been darkened, and by the passions the lamp has been quenched, Savior. But have pity and give me back, as David sings, the [?]
Turn back, repent, uncover what is hidden. Say to God, who knows all things: You alone know my secrets, Savior. Have mercy on me yourself, as David sings, according to your mercy [?]
My days have passed away like the dream of one who wakes. So, like Hezekiah, I weep on my bed that years of life may be added to me. But what Isaiah will stand by you, O soul, if not the God of all?

You once cried out to the immaculate Mother of God and drove back the frenzy of the passions that were violently troubling you, and you put to shame the enemy who had tripped you up. Now grant help in affliction to me too, your servant. He whom you loved, whom you longed for, in whose footsteps you followed [?], found your repentance and granted it, for he alone is the compassionate God. Entreat him unceasingly that we may be delivered from passions and adversities. Another reading: “elders.” Another reading: “become like the woman of Zarephath.” [?]
Simple, undivided, consubstantial Trinity, one nature, Lights and Light, three holy and one Holy: the Trinity is hymned as God. Hymn and glorify, O soul, the Life and the Lives, the God of all.

We hymn you, we bless you, we worship you, Mother of God, for you bore the one Son and God of the inseparable Trinity, and you yourself opened the things of heaven to us on earth. The Triodion. Plagal tone 4. Ode 8. The Irmos. The King of glory without beginning, before whom the powers of heaven shudder and the ranks of angels tremble: hymn him, you priests and people. O apostles, like coals of immaterial fire, burn up my material passions, and kindle in me now a longing for divine love. Let us honor the sweet-sounding trumpets of the Word, by which the enemy's unfounded walls fell and the battlements of the knowledge of God were firmly set. Sanctified apostles of the Lord, you who smashed the enemy's temples and pillars, smash the passionate idols of my soul.

Another [canon] [?]. The same irmos. Apostles of Christ, you built the whole Church by the architecture of the Spirit: in it bless Christ forever. Sounding the trumpets of doctrine, the apostles overthrew all idolatrous error, exalting Christ above all for all ages. Apostles, noble colony, overseers of the world and citizens of heaven, rescue from dangers those who always praise you. Andrew's. [Glory.] Thrice-radiant, all-shining Godhead, nature of equal glory and equal throne, Father, maker of all, Son and divine Spirit: I hymn you forever. Both now. Theotokion. Let us hymn the Mother of God unceasingly, O peoples, as an honored and most exalted throne, the only one who after giving birth is both mother and virgin. Another irmos. Another irmos. Him whom the hosts of heaven glorify, before whom tremble the

8. ANDREW OF CRETE. Cherubim and the Seraphim: every breath and creature, hymn, bless and exalt him above all forever. Have mercy on me, a sinner, Savior. Rouse my mind to conversion. Receive me as I repent, and have pity on me as I cry: Against you alone have I sinned; I have transgressed; have mercy on me. Elijah the charioteer once mounted the chariot of the virtues and was carried up as if to heaven, high above earthly things. Consider his ascent, then, my soul. Elisha once parted the stream of the Jordan this way and that with Elijah's mantle. But you, my soul, have had no share in this grace through [?]

When Elisha once received the mantle, he received a double grace from the Lord. But you, O my soul, have had no share in this grace, because of your lack of self-control. The Shunammite woman once welcomed the righteous man as a guest with good will, O soul. But you have taken into your house neither stranger nor traveler. So you will be thrown out of the bridal chamber, lamenting. Wretched soul, you have always imitated the foul mind of Gehazi. Throw off his love of money, at least in old age. Flee the fire of Gehenna and turn away from your evils. You have emulated Uzziah, O soul, and you have his leprosy in you twice over, for you think absurd things and do lawless ones. Let go of what you hold, and run to [?]

You have heard, O soul, of the Ninevites who repented before God in sackcloth and ashes. You did not imitate them; instead you have shown yourself more perverse than all who offended before the law and after the law. You have heard, O soul, of Jeremiah in the muddy pit, crying out in laments against the city of Zion and seeking tears. Imitate his life of lamentation, and you will be saved. Jonah ran away to Tarshish, because he foresaw that the Ninevites would turn back. As a prophet he knew God's compassion, so he was anxious that his prophecy should not be proved false. You have heard, O soul, how Daniel in the den stopped the mouths of the beasts. You know how the youths with Azariah quenched by faith the flame of the furnace [?]

I have brought before you, O soul, everyone in the Old Testament as a pattern. Imitate the God-loving deeds of the righteous, and flee in turn the sins of the wicked. Savior, righteous Judge, have mercy, and rescue me from the fire and from the threat I must justly suffer at the judgment. Forgive me before the end, through virtue and repent[ance] [?]

I weep bitterly. “Forgive me, Saviour,” I cry like the tax collector; I weep like the harlot; accept my lament, as you once accepted that of the Canaanite woman. Heal, Saviour, the festering of my lowly soul; only Physician, lay a poultice on me, and oil and wine: works of repentance, compunction with [?]

Even if no one has sinned against you as I have, yet accept me too, compassionate Saviour, as I repent in fear and cry out in longing: “Against you alone have I sinned, I have done wrong; have mercy on me.” Spare, Saviour, your own creature, and seek out the lost sheep as a shepherd; snatch me from the wolf when I have strayed; make me a nursling in the fold of your sheep. When you sit as Judge, compassionate as you are, and show your fearful glory, O Christ, what fear there will be then! The furnace will be burning, and all will cower before the unbearable terror of your judgment seat.

The Mother of the never-setting Light enlightened you and freed you from the darkness of the passions. Therefore, Mary, since you have received the grace of the Spirit, enlighten those who faithfully praise you. Zosimas, truly a man of God, was astonished, Mother, when he beheld a new wonder in you; for he saw an angel in a body, and was wholly filled with amazement, praising Christ unto the ages.

Since you have boldness before the Lord, Andrew, revered glory of Crete, I implore you: intercede, that by your prayers I may now find release from the bond of my lawlessness, for you are the teacher of repentance and the glory of the saints. We bless the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. Father without beginning, Son co-eternal with him, good Comforter, upright Spirit; Begetter of God the Word, Word of the Father without beginning, Spirit living and creating; Trinity, Unity, have mercy on me.

The Triodion. Tone [?]. Ode 4 [?]. Truly, Mother of God, we confess you, we who have been saved through you, pure Virgin; with the choirs of the bodiless ones we magnify you. Apostles, you who were revealed as springs of the saving stream, you have bedewed my soul, which was wasting away with the thirst of sin. Swimming in the sea of destruction, and already [?], with your right hand, Lord, as you did Peter, [?]

[?] those who praise you with longing. [?] Glory. You, the Unity in three Persons, Father, Son, [?] with the Spirit, one consubstantial God, we praise, a Trinity [?] and without beginning. You, the Mother of the Child and Virgin, all generations [?]

for you bore the Lord for us. Of the Great Canon. Heirmos. [?] incorruptible is the conception [?] for the birth [?]. The mind is wounded; the body [?] [?] what will you do when the [Judge?] comes to search out your deeds? [?] Moses' account [of the] creation of the world, [?] and from it all the covenanted Scripture, which recounts to you the righteous and the unrighteous; of these, O soul, you have imitated the second and not the first, sinning against God. [?]

[?] and every word of the righteous [?]. Your wounds, O soul, have multiplied, and there is no physician to heal you. I bring before you the examples of the New Scripture, to lead you, soul, to compunction. Emulate, then, the righteous; turn away from the sinners; and win Christ's favour with prayers and fasting, with purity and reverence. Christ became man, sharing my flesh; and he fulfilled all that belongs to human nature, apart from sin, setting before you, O soul, the pattern and image of his condescension. Christ became man and called robbers and harlots to repentance. Repent, soul: the door of the kingdom has already been opened, and Pharisees, tax collectors, and adulterers who change their ways are seizing it before you. Christ saved the Magi; he called the shepherds together; he made throngs of infants martyrs; he glorified an old man and an aged widow; yet, soul, you have not emulated their deeds or their life. But woe to you at the [?]

The desert-loving turtledove, the voice of one crying out, Christ's lamp, sounded forth, preaching repentance. Herod acted lawlessly, together with his Herodias. Take care, my soul, that you are not caught in the snares of the lawless, but embrace repentance. The Forerunner of grace dwelt in the desert, and all Judea and Samaria heard him and ran to him and confessed their sins, eagerly receiving baptism; but you, soul, did not imitate them. Marriage is honourable, and the marriage bed undefiled; for Christ blessed both beforehand, eating in the flesh, and at the wedding in Cana turning water into wine and showing his first miracle, so that you, wretched soul, might be saved.

Christ raised up the paralytic, who took up his bed. [?] and [the servant] of the centurion; and to the Samaritan woman [?] he prefigured for you, soul, worship in spirit. The Lord healed the woman with the flow of blood through the touch of his hem; he cleansed lepers; he gave light to the blind and set the lame upright; the deaf and the mute, and the woman bent to the ground, he healed by his word, so that you [?] might be saved. Christ the Word healed diseases and preached good news to the poor; he cured the crippled; he ate with tax collectors; he kept company with sinners; [he restored] the soul of Jairus's daughter, which had already departed, by the touch of his hand.

The tax collector was saved, and the harlot came to her senses, and the boastful Pharisee was condemned; for the one cried, “Be merciful [to me],” and the other, “Have mercy on me,” but the third boasted, crying, “O God, I thank you,” and the rest [?]. Zacchaeus was a tax collector, yet he was saved; but Simon the Pharisee went astray, and the harlot received release and forgiveness from him who has the power to forgive sins. Win his favour for yourself, soul. You have not emulated the harlot, O my wretched soul, who took the alabaster jar of myrrh and with tears anointed the Lord's feet and wiped them with her hair, while he tore up for her the record of her old offences. You know, [soul?], how the cities to which Christ gave the Gospel were cursed. Fear the example, lest you become like them; for the Master likened them to the people of Sodom and condemned them to Hades. Do not show yourself worse, O my soul, through [despair?], when you have heard of the faith of the Canaanite woman, through which her little daughter was healed by the word of God. Cry out from the depth of your heart, “Son of God, save me too,” as she cried [?]

“Have compassion; save me, Son of David,” [to him who?] healed the demon-possessed by a word. [?] [You said?] to the thief [?]: “Amen, I say to you, you will be with me in paradise when I come in my glory.” One thief reproached you; the other confessed your divinity; for both hung with you on the cross. But, O most compassionate one, as you did for the faithful thief who knew you to be God, open to me too the door of your glorious kingdom. Creation was shaken as it saw you crucified; mountains and rocks were split with fear; and Hades was [?] [?] Matthew 15:22. Luke [?]

laid bare; and the light was darkened in the daytime as it beheld you, Jesus, nailed in the flesh. Do not demand of me fruits worthy of repentance, for my strength has failed within me. Grant me a heart ever contrite, and poverty of spirit, so that I may offer these to you as an acceptable sacrifice, only [?]

My Judge, who knows me, who are to come again with the angels to judge the whole world: then look on me with your merciful eye, and spare me and pity me, Jesus, for I have sinned beyond all human nature. Of the Saint. You amazed everyone by your strange way of life, both the ranks of angels and the assemblies of mortals; for you lived [?] and surpassed nature, and so, Mary, treading [?] with your feet, you crossed the Jordan. Win the Creator's favour, holy Mother, for those who praise you, that we may be delivered from the afflictions and tribulations that beset us on every side; so that, delivered from temptations, we may unceasingly magnify the one who glorified you, [?]

Andrew, venerable and thrice-blessed Father, shepherd of Crete, do not cease to pray for those who sing your praises, that we who faithfully honour you may be delivered from all wrath and affliction, from corruption, and from countless [?] offences.

Consubstantial Trinity, Unity in three Persons, we praise you, glorifying the Father, magnifying the Son, and worshipping the Spirit, the one God truly by nature, life and lives, a kingdom without end.

Guard your city, immaculate Mother of God; for in you it reigns faithfully, and in you it is made strong; and conquering through you, it routs every trial, despoils its enemies, and governs its subjects [?]

At Compline we sing the present canon of Andrew of Crete, the Jerusalemite. Ode 1. Tone 1. Heirmos. Let us all sing a song of victory to God, who worked marvellous wonders with a high arm and saved Israel, for he has been glorified. Having raised the man four days dead, my Saviour, [Note 19: “Life and lives” (Latin: vitamque et vitas).]

Lazarus, [you snatched him?] from corruption with a high arm, and showed your authority as the Mighty One. You called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him up [?]; but Hades below [?] bitterly, and groaning, trembled, Saviour, at your authority. You wept, Lord, over Lazarus, revealing the incarnation of your saving plan, and that, being God by nature, you became by nature a man like us. You ended the tears of Martha and of Mary, Lord, by raising Lazarus from the dead, Saviour, and showing the dead man breathing again by the authority [?]

Without change, Virgin Mother, you conceived the Creator of nature by the Holy Spirit, through the good pleasure of the Father; he became what we are, without change and [?]. Ode 2. Heirmos. Give heed, O heaven, and I will speak, and I will sing the praises of Christ the Saviour of the world, the only lover of mankind [?]

Glory to you, who by a mere call raise from the tomb your friend Lazarus, four days dead. The breathless man heard your voice, and, receiving his soul again, rose at once from the dead, glorifying you, Lord. Receiving the command of your life-giving voice, the man who stank rose from the tomb, my Saviour, [?]
Hades trembled as it saw the man bound in grave-bands running straight back up at the voice [calling him] here [?]

The storehouses of Hades were shaken when Lazarus [?] at once below, at the voice of him who gives life. Ode 3. Heirmos. The stone which the builders rejected has become the head of the corner. This is the rock on which Christ established his Church, which he purchased from the nations. A strange and astonishing wonder: how the Creator of all, as though he did not know what he knew full well, asked, “Where does he lie whom you mourn? Where is Lazarus buried, whom in a little while I shall raise from the dead and give back to you alive?” The stone that your mourners had rolled against you, Jesus ordered to be moved, and at once raised you, calling to you: “Lazarus, arise; come here to me,” so that Hades might cower at your voice. Martha and Mary cried out with lamentation, Lord: “See, the one you loved stinks on the fourth day. If you had been here then, Lazarus would not have died.” But since you are absent from nothing, you called him and at once raised him. Shedding tears over a friend for the sake of your saving plan, you showed that the flesh taken from us was united to you in reality and not in appearance, Saviour; and as God who loves mankind, you called him and at once raised him. “Alas! Now I am truly lost!” Hades cried out, and thus addressed Death: “Look, the Nazarene has shaken the regions below, and has split open my belly, and by a call has raised a breathless corpse.” Where is the folly of the Hebrews? Where is their unbelief? How long, you deceivers? How long, you bastards? You see the dead man leaping out at a voice, and you do not believe in Christ? Truly you are all sons of darkness.

I know you as one of the Trinity, even though you became flesh; and I glorify the one incarnate Son, who sprang without seed from the Mother of God, and who with the Father and the Spirit is glorified as the one Son. Strange and awesome is the vision, by God's saving plan, which the truthful prophets foresaw: a Virgin Mother of God, conceiving without seed, giving birth to God without seed, and remaining pure after childbirth. Ode 4. Heirmos. The sun was lifted up, and the moon stood still in its course. You were lifted up on the tree, long-suffering one, and on it you made your Church firm. You wept, Lord, over Lazarus, showing that you are man; and you raised the dead man, Master, and showed the peoples that you are the Son of God. The breathless man heard your command, “Lazarus, come out!”; he rose up running, with his grave-wrappings, and leapt, good Lord, displaying your might. The tears of Martha and of Mary [you] [?]

Weeping as man over Lazarus, you raised him up as God. You asked where the man four days dead was buried, confirming, good Lord, your incarnation. Wishing to make known the signs of your passion and your cross, good Lord, you tore open the insatiable belly of Hades and as God raised the man four days dead. Who has seen, who has heard, that a dead man who already stank has risen? Elijah raised the dead, and Elisha too, but not from a tomb, nor on the fourth day. We praise your power, Lord; we praise your sufferings too, O Christ; for by the one, in your compassion, you worked wonders, and the others, for the sake of your saving plan, you [?]

You are God and man, making the names true by deeds; you, the Word, came in the flesh to the tomb, and as God raised the man four days dead. The crowds of the Hebrews were astonished, Master, when they saw Lazarus risen from the tomb at your voice, and yet they remained unbelieving of your wonders.

The conception of the Mother of God was without seed; the birth was without the passion of corruption. For God, having worked both these wonders, emptied himself to be united with us. Ode 5. Heirmos. Give us your peace, Son of God; for we know no other God beside you, since you are God of the living and the dead. Being life and light, Lord, [?] you called Lazarus and raised him; for as the Mighty One you showed all that you are God of the living and the dead. Unable to bear your irresistible command, Jesus, Hades, which had received many, cowered; and Lazarus, who had been four days dead, at the voice [came forth] alive and no longer dead [?]

Word of life, you who of old joined dust with spirit and gave life to the clay by your word, now too by a word you have raised your friend from corruption and from the regions beneath the earth. No one has withstood your nod, Lord. So when you called the dead Lazarus, at once the breathless man rose, and, still wearing his bonds, walked about on his feet. O folly of the Jews! O hardness of the enemies! Who has ever seen one raising the dead from the tomb? Elijah raised the dead of old, but not from a tomb, nor on the fourth day.
Your immaculate womb, pure one, was sanctified when he who is beyond God took flesh from it, the Word from the Father, worshipped in Trinity [?], and with the Spirit [?]

Ode 6. Heirmos. You cast me into the depths of the heart of the sea, and saved me, Saviour, from the slavery of death, and loosed the bond of my iniquities. You asked where I was, you who know [all things?]; you wept for me, Saviour, being man by nature, and raised me from the dead by your command. “You called me from lowest Hades, Saviour,” Lazarus cries to you, the destroyer of Hades, “and raised me from the dead by your command. You clothed me, Saviour, with a body of clay, and breathed life into me, and I saw your light; and you raised me from the dead by your command. You [gave soul to?] the breathless form of my flesh; you bound me together with bones and sinews; and you raised me from the dead by your command. Tearing open the all-devouring belly of Hades, you snatched me out, Saviour, by your power, and raised me from the dead by your command.” You put on, Saviour, the whole of my human dough; and you kept pure the immaculate womb from which you came forth incarnate, being one of the Trinity.

The Word entered your immaculate womb, Mother of God, and after his birth kept it pure once more: a truly astonishing wonder. Ode 7. Heirmos. The fire did not touch your children in the furnace, Saviour, nor did it harm them; then the three, as with one mouth, sang hymns and blessed you, saying: Blessed is the God of our fathers. You wept over the dead, Saviour, lover of mankind, to show all the peoples that, being God, you appeared as man for our sake. And you wept willingly, setting before us examples of heartfelt love. When Lazarus, four days dead, heard your voice below, Saviour, he arose and sang your praises; and rejoicing,

he cried: “You are my God and Creator; I worship and praise you who raised me.” “Though I am wrapped in bonds,” Lazarus cried from below, “Redeemer, I will by no means remain in the belly of Hades, if only you call me: ‘Lazarus, come out.’ For you are my light and life.” “I beg you, Lazarus,” says [Hades], “rise up and get out of my bars quickly. Away with you, then! For it is better for me to bewail bitterly the loss of one than of all whom I swallowed before in my hunger.” “And why do you delay, Lazarus?” he says. “Your friend is crying, ‘Come here!’ So stand up, that I too may have some relief; for ever since I ate you, my food has turned to vomit for me.” “Why do you not get up quickly, Lazarus?” Hades cried out from below, lamenting. “Why do you not rise at once and run from here, lest Christ, in raising you, take others captive from me too?” You were marvelled at, Master Christ, when you then worked many extraordinary deeds: by a word you opened light to the blind and ears to the deaf, and as God you called your friend Lazarus and raised him from the dead.
Let us sing a hymn to the Trinity, glorifying the Father without beginning, and the Son, and the upright Spirit, one single essence, whom let us praise threefold: Holy, holy, holy are you, O Trinity.

We glorify you, Christ, as one of the Trinity, because you took flesh from the Virgin without change and endured all things as a man, without departing from your Father's nature, Jesus, even though you were united with us. Ode 8. Heirmos. Heavens of heavens, and the water above the heavens, bless, praise, and exalt the Lord above all for ever. The maker and sustainer of all things came in his compassion to Bethany to raise Lazarus.

[?] four days dead and stinking, and bound with grave-bands, the breathless man leapt up breathing when you called. When the people of the Jews saw the dead man risen at your voice, Christ, they were cut to the heart [?]. O Jews, in darkness before the light, why do you not believe in the raising of Lazarus? It is the work of Christ. Let Zion rejoice and praise the giver of life, who by a word raised Lazarus from the tomb. The armies of heaven and the race of those born of earth sang your praises when, my Saviour, [you raised] Lazarus [?]
With the Father and the Son I glorify the Spirit too, and in praise I cry without ceasing: Thrice-holy One, glory to you.

I bless and worship you who were born of the Virgin, yet never separated from the throne of your holy glory. Ode 9. Heirmos. He has shown strength with his arm; for he has brought down the mighty from their thrones and lifted up the lowly, the God of Israel, in whom the Dawn from on high has visited us and guided us into the way of peace. Let Bethany sing the wonder with us; for there the Creator wept, by the law of the nature of the flesh, when he raised Lazarus; and then, turning Martha's tears and Mary's weeping into joy, he raises the dead man. Confirming your own resurrection, O Word, you called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him as God, to show the peoples that you are at once truly God and man, and the one who would raise the temple of [your] body.

Of old you shattered the iron bars as well; you terrified Hades with your voice, and Death cowered at once with it, when they saw Lazarus, Saviour, their prisoner, given life again by your voice and risen. All were astonished when they saw you, Saviour, weeping for the dead Lazarus, and those cruel men said, “See how he loved him!” At once, then, you called him, and the breathless man rose and put off corruption at your command. The gates were shaken, the bars were broken, the bonds of the dead man were loosed; and Hades, at the voice of Christ's power, groaned bitterly and cried out: “Alas! Who is this, and where does this voice come from that gives life to the dead? Rise up from here, obey the voice; for your friend is calling to you outside. This is he who in times past raised the dead. Elijah raised a dead man, and Elisha too; but it was he who through them both spoke and acted.” We praise your incomparable strength, O Word; for by your word you raised the dead man with bones and sinews, as the fashioner of all things; and you raised him, Saviour, from the regions beneath the earth, as you did the widow's son on his bier.

All-holy Trinity, God the Father without beginning, Son co-eternal and divine Word, good Comforter, Holy Spirit of God; one light shining as three suns, one essence of the same nature, one God and Lord, have pity on the world.

Jesus, who made all things in wisdom, and put on the whole of me from the Virgin, while remaining wholly and for ever in the bosom of the Father: as God, Christ, send down your Holy Spirit upon your flock and overshadow us. [Notes:] Another reading: “you broke.” Perhaps: “you bound together.”

On Palm Sunday, in the evening, at Compline. [?] We chant the Triodion of the Lord [?] [?] of Great Week, in the evening, at Compline. Ode 1, plagal fourth tone. "To him who shattered cities." Let us, the faithful, imitate the chastity of Joseph, [?] who honored [?] the redeeming nature [?] of humankind, as we live in all watchfulness by active virtue. Neglect of good works was likened to the fig tree. So let us avoid it, or we will be punished as that tree was then: the synagogue, thick with leaves [?]. Jesus [?] for the world [?]. Willingly he goes up with his disciples to the city of Jerusalem, to his voluntary passion, [?]

Clinging to the Lord who hastens to suffer all things, let us be ready for mockery, for spitting, for scorn, so that we, the faithful, may be glorified with him in his immaculate sufferings. He who suffered for us heals sufferings by sufferings. Willingly he accepts, in the human [?] that is ours, [?] his sufferings, that we may be saved.
I glorify three without beginning; I hymn three who are holy; I proclaim three co-eternal [?] in one [?]. For one God is glorified in Father, [?] Son and [?]. The rod of Moses and the rod of Aaron

[?] underwent a strange transformation, and a dispensation beyond understanding [?]. But your womb, Mother of God, makes a new birth. Kathisma, tone 4. "You have appeared today." Do not let the charge brought against the fig tree overtake you, O soul. Instead hasten to bring [?] fruits of the heart to Christ your Maker, offering them to him in repentance. Ode 8. "Him whom they glorified on the holy mountain." Let us adorn our life with temperance and guard the faith with prudence. Let us gain the ways of justice, so that, following Christ with courage, we may be crucified with him. The patriarch Joseph found in the Egyptian woman another Eve, but he was not lured into impiety. He stood like a diamond and was not captured by the passions of the [?]. As you passed along the roads of this life, O my Savior, you hungered by your own will, longing for the salvation of all. This is what you hungered for: the return of those who had strayed from you. When our forefather had tasted of the tree and knew that he was naked and ashamed, he took fig leaves and girded himself, prefiguring the synagogue stripped bare of Christ. Prepare yourself, O soul, before your departure; make ready for the life to come. Christ hastens to suffer for you so that he may glorify you; so hasten to suffer with him, to die with him and be crucified with him. How could death not shudder, O my Savior? How could Hades not cower when it met you, hastening of your own good pleasure to the passion and seeing that you had come to suffer for the unjust? The Jews, priests and Levites, saw the raising of Lazarus and in their envy contrived a conspiracy. By treacherous guile they handed Christ over to Pilate to be put to death. Your ewe-lamb, your handmaid and virgin, saw you rushing to the passion, the good shepherd laying down his life for us, and with a mother's heart she was pierced with grief for you.

The Mother of God implores you, O Christ; the company of the disciples entreats you: Grant your peace to your world, and bestow your compassions richly on us forever. Ode 9. "Virginity is foreign to mothers." Chastity is foreign to the indecent, and lawlessness is strange to the just. But the great Joseph turned away from sin and became a byword for chastity, truly an image and type of Christ. [?] 11:47 ff.; John [?]; Gen. [?]

Lawful order is foreign to the lawless, and the knowledge of God is strange to the faithless. The Jews rejected these things through lawlessness, and so they alone inherited the curse, like the fig tree. He hungered for the salvation of humankind, he who is the bread of life, Christ my God. [?] Coming upon the fig tree, the fruitless synagogue luxuriant with the leaves of the law, he saw it and cursed it. You cursed in advance the fruitlessness of the law, which blossomed like leaves with the shadowy sense of the letter but had no fruits of works because of lawlessness. But all of us, the sons of grace, you have blessed, O Savior. The rod of Moses formerly [?] into [?]; Aaron's rod put forth green [?] leaves, though it was fruitless and withered. But the lawless synagogue was changed into a fruitless [?]

Make ready your priests, O Judea; prepare your hands for the killing of God. For behold, he has come to the passion meek and quiet: he who is the Lamb and our Shepherd, Christ the King of Israel. Receive your king, O Judea. Behold, he comes willingly to the passion, that he may suffer and save those who cry without ceasing: "Blessed is he who comes [?] by the cross to save all things." He has turned your feasts [?], O Judea, [?] the Master [?], according to the prophecy [?]; [?] you were seen, [?] of him who once turned the [?]

It is foreign to the lawless to glorify you, the essence without beginning, Father and Son and Holy Spirit, the uncreated almighty rule, by which [?] the world is established, by the nod of God [?] its might.

Ode 2. The heirmos. Attend, O heaven, and I will speak, and I will hymn Christ, who came to dwell among us in the flesh from a Virgin. Attend, O heaven, and I will speak; give ear, O earth, to a voice [?]. I too offer the tears of the harlot, O compassionate one; [?] me, O Savior, in your tender mercy. I have darkened the beauty of my soul [?] with the pleasures of the passions, and [?] I have turned my whole mind to dust. I have now torn my first robe, which the Creator wove for me in the beginning, and so I lie naked and I am ashamed.

Immaculate Mother of God, Virgin, alone all-praised, entreat your Son for your servants. Another heirmos. The same tone. See, see that I am God, who knew all things before anything came to be, before the earth and the heaven were established; who am wholly in the Father and bear him wholly in me. See, see that I am God, who of old led Israel through the Red Sea, saved him, fed him, and freed him from slavery.

By a word I established heaven together with earth, for I was with the Father; and by a word I bear this universe, as Word and Wisdom and Power and Image, co-worker and equal in working. Who set the times? Who preserves the ages? Who bounds the universe and moves it, if not he who without beginning is ever with the Father, like a ray in the light? O your measureless love for mankind, Jesus! From above you made known to us the season of the consummation, hiding the hour but making its signs plain and clear. You understand all things, you know all things, Jesus, for you have divinely in yourself the dignity of the Father, and you bear in yourself by nature the whole Spirit, co-eternal
Master and Lord, maker of the ages, count us too worthy to hear on that day the holy voice calling the elect of the Father into the kingdom of heaven.
Trinity without beginning and uncreated, undivided unity, being three and one, Father, Son and Spirit, one God: accept this hymn from tongues of clay as though from mouths of flame.

You were shown to be a divine tabernacle, O Virgin of God. For the King of the heavens dwelt in you bodily and came forth in beauty, divinely refashioning humanity in himself. Kathisma, tone 2. "Of compassion." Moved by compassion, O Christ, you come willingly to suffer, O Benefactor, wishing to redeem us from the passions and from condemnation in Hades. Therefore we all hymn your precious sufferings, and we glorify, O Savior, your supreme condescension. Ode 8. The heirmos. Angels and heavens, bless, hymn and exalt above all, forever, him who rides upon the throne of glory and is glorified without ceasing as God

to his disciples, he foretold the consummation, saying [?]. Now that you know your end, prepare yourself from now on; it comes without [?]. You have learned, barren soul, the [?] of the wicked servant. Be afraid, and do not neglect the gift you received, which was given you not to hide in the earth but to trade with. Let the lamp be made bright and let its oil overflow, as compassion did for the virgins then, so that you may find, my soul, the bridal chamber open on that day. When the Teacher spoke of flight on the Sabbath and in winter, [he signified] the storm of the seventh [age] [?] of the present age, in which he will return, like a winter

You have heard, my soul, that the fearful coming of your Master will be like the swiftness of lightning flashing across the sky; so hasten now to be ready. When the Judge comes with thousands and myriads of angelic ranks and powers, what fear there will be, my soul! What trembling! Alas! As we stand naked
So the Trinity is one God. The Father does not pass over into youth [?], nor is the Son changed into procession; but each in his own way, and both [?] light, the three as God I glorify unto [?]

You have heard, O soul, the Judge proclaiming in advance and teaching you the time of the consummation. Prepare the works you need for your departure, so that you are not rejected by God as one who failed the test. Learn the end from the fig tree, O soul: when its leaves grow tender and it puts out branches, the hour of summer is at hand. So you too, when you see these things, know that [it is near] at

that Adam may be saved. The great and divine Pascha has drawn near. For Christ teaches beforehand that after two days, marking out in advance the day of his passion, [he who is] in the Father is offered as a sacrifice. Standing by your cross, O Savior, your Mother saw your unjust slaughter and cried out: "Alas, my Child! Light that never sets, shine upon all, Sun of glory, the light!"
O Unity, holy Trinity, the one Godhead; Trinity in unity, God, nature in three hypostases, glory equal in honor and undivided: rescue the souls of [?]

Accept your Mother as intercessor, O Christ, so that through her supplications you may give peace to the world, strengthen the sceptres of the kingdom and join your churches into one. On Holy and Great Tuesday, at Compline, we chant the Triodion of the Lord Andrew. Ode [?], tone 2. The heirmos. O God, husbandman of good things and planter of what is good, in your tender mercy make my barren mind fruitful. It is the time of the consummation; let us turn back now, Christ teaches. For he will come in an instant; he will come and will not delay, to judge his world. [?] Showing how sudden his coming will be, Christ spoke of the unexpected destruction that once came upon the earth in the days of Noah. The bridal chamber has been opened, and the divine wedding has been made ready along with it. The Bridegroom is near and calls us; let us make ourselves ready [?]. Simon's dwelling held you, whom nothing can contain, O Jesus our King, and a sinful woman anointed you with myrrh. Filled with mystical fragrance, the woman was rescued, O Savior, from the former stench of her many sins, for you pour forth the myrrh of life. Though you yourself are heavenly food and the life of the hungry, you were entertained at table by men, O Christ, showing forth your condescension. B. Enough has been said about this too. Now tell me: how did he deliver us from sin?
A. What is sin? Is it not a kind of failure, a missing of the mark? Think of a healthy person: when he walks, he puts his foot down wherever he wants. But if some weakness makes him ill and he becomes shaky, he cannot put his foot where he wants. He aims to plant his step on a certain spot, but the illness within him pushes him, and his foot turns aside somewhere else. In the same way sin, once it has settled in our soul, has made the soul weak and sick, so that it misses and falls short of its proper aims and purposes. But Christ baptizes us in water and the Spirit, and the grace of the Holy Spirit strengthens us. It scrapes away all sin, sickness and disease. It renews us, makes us new again, and restores us to the strength and beauty we had of old, before the transgression.
B. The fifth point remains, the one about Hades.
A. It was impossible for the Lord to dwell with his flesh among those in Hades. So when death separated the Lord's soul from his flesh, his soul went without the body to dwell among the souls in darkness. It flashed the light of the Godhead upon them, moved those who believed in him into paradise, and destroyed the kingdom of Hades. Just as the all-holy Virgin became the gate and entrance through which God the Word came into the world, so death became the gate and entrance through which he went down into Hades.

A distinction and clarification of the terms that occupy the philosophers, and a refutation of the soul-destroying heresy of the Acephalous Severians, that is, the Jacobites, by the same Abu Qurrah.

Those who love and defend the true doctrines need to distinguish and clarify the terms that especially occupy the philosophers. Many who seem to be wise did not know these terms precisely, and so they missed the truth, ran aground on absurdities and blasphemies, and fell away from right faith in God. They were ignorant, but willingly so: they turned the eyes of their minds away from the light of salvation, deserted to the deadly darkness, and slid into the pit of perdition. We will therefore leave aside for now any discussion of meaningless sounds, whether articulate, or inarticulate and conveying meaning inarticulately, since these contribute nothing to the method of demonstration. Instead we will speak briefly about the terms themselves, as far as we are able. In this way we will arm the Church's nurslings against the Church's deranged opponents, the Acephalous heretics, and we will refute their folly and feebleness and expose it publicly.

On the Sabbaths, and on every day, Christ performed the works of his signs, healing those who suffered from all kinds of diseases. But the misled people nursed a grudge in their anger. "This man," they said, "healed this paralytic on the Sabbath, a man who had lain sick for very many years, and so he broke the law." So the Jews bitterly abused Christ. "Did not Moses, who gave you the law," he said, "command you to circumcise? And you circumcise a man on the Sabbath" [?].

Ode 9. Heirmos: "A thing foreign to mothers."
When the feast of the Jews was half over, O my Savior, you went up to your temple and taught everyone [?]. The Jews were amazed and said, "How does this man know letters when he has never studied?"
My Redeemer poured out healings as gifts. He performed wonders and signs, drove away diseases and healed the sick. But the Jews raged at how many miracles he worked.
My Redeemer rebuked the disobedient Jews and cried out: "Do not judge by appearances, but judge with righteous judgment." For the law commands every man to be circumcised even on the Sabbath.
